call_points.text: Presentation names fuel volatility, forex volatility and supply chain disruptions as key risks.
Capacity to grow around 3-4% in Q1FY27 versus the same period last year.
Unit passenger revenue seen up mid-teens in Q1FY27, helped by fuel charges and a low base.
CASK ex-fuel ex-forex expected in mid- to high single digits, with volatility caveat.
Total cash of around ₹51,600 Cr at year end, of which ₹36,200 Cr is free cash.
Plans to keep ₹20,000-25,000 Cr as a liquidity safety net and deploy the rest into aircraft ownership.
Prepaying finance lease obligations of USD 450 million to the GIFT City entity for aircraft and engine acquisition.
No dividend recommended for FY2026 given the year's financial performance and distributable reserves.
Pratt & Whitney groundings in the 40s, expected to fall into the 30s by year end.
Middle East and Europe are about 18% of capacity and roughly 160 daily flights; two-thirds restored.
Management says it has not fully passed on the fuel increase, especially internationally.
No full-year ASK guidance; management will give only quarterly guidance for now.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has disputed Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) levied by Customs authorities on re-import of aircraft, engines & certain aircraft parts after performing repair outside India. With respect to IGST paid on imports prior to 19 July 2021, the Company has received favourable orders from CESTAT- New Delhi, which were appealed by the Department before the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India. On July 14, 2025 the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India dismissed one (1) out of three (3) pending appeals filed by the Department. Further, the Government vide Notification dated July 19, 2021 amended the customs notification to re-iterate their position that IGST is applicable on re-import of goods after repair. The Company filed a Writ Petition before the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi challenging the constitutional validity of the Amendment Notification. On March 4, 2025 Hon’ble High Court of Delhi pronounced its order, holding that repair and re-import transaction is a supply of service and levy of IGST at the time of re-import of goods repaired abroad is unconstitutional and invalid. Department has filed appeal before the Hon’ble Supreme Court on August 29, 2025 against the order dated March 4, 2025 passed by the Hon’ble High Court of Delhi. The last update in this regard was provided as a part of Integrated filing - Governance submitted for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Deputy Commissioner /Assistant Commissioner /Joint Commissioner of Custom - New Delhi/Bengaluru/ Hyderabad/Chennai /Mumbai
tax_litigation.status: Department had filed review petition against dismissal of department’s appeal by Hon’ble Supreme Court on July 14, 2025. Such review petition was dismissed by Hon’ble Supreme Court on February 17, 2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: On December 29, 2025, the GST authorities erroneously raised GST demand of INR 4,583 mn on compensation received from foreign supplier and also denied Input Tax credit. The Company was in process of contesting the Order before the appropriate forum. The stock exchange disclosure in this regard was made on December 30, 2025.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Additional Commissioner of CGST- Delhi South Commissionerate

entities.name: InterGlobe Aviation Financial Services IFSC Private Limited

operating_notes.text: Received DGCA warning letter regarding December 2025 airfares under temporary caps; refunds completed with no financial impact.
FY26 forex loss of ₹8,975.7 Cr against ₹1,617.9 Cr in FY25, driven by rupee movement on aircraft and lease liabilities.
Cumulative IGST paid under protest on re-import of repaired aircraft reached ₹22,028 million at 31 March 2026, shown as recoverable.
DGCA penalty of ₹222 million paid on 16 February 2026 and ₹500 million bank guarantees furnished for reforms.
Partial prepayment of finance lease obligations up to USD 450 million approved.
IndiGo damp leased six Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners from Norse Atlantic Airways in early 2025 as a bridge to its own Airbus A350 long-haul fleet.
One of the six Boeing 787-9s will be returned to Norse Atlantic Airways after the Manchester route is discontinued from 31 August 2026; the remaining long-haul flights continue as planned.
Fleet stood at 441 aircraft at end-FY26 after 51 orderbook inductions and 21 damp leases, offset by 37 orderbook and 28 damp-lease redeliveries.
Middle East and Europe represent around 18% of total capacity and approximately 160 daily flights; about two-thirds were operating again by the call.
FY26 passenger unit revenue (PRASK) for Q4 came in at ₹4.46, 4% lower year on year on a high Maha-Kumbh base.
IndiGo temporarily suspended operations to Langkawi, Krabi, Ho Chi Minh, Hong Kong, Shanghai and Siem Reap from July to September 2026.
Fleet at 31 March 2026 was 441 aircraft with 901 yet to be delivered; 9 A321 XLR deliveries expected in FY27.
CASK ex fuel ex forex was USD 4.08 cents, stage-length adjusted, against 3.11-9.94 cents for other LCCs in Jan-Dec 2025.
Free cash balance of ₹362 bn (USD 3.8 bn) at FY26 end.
Fuel CASK rose about 80% YoY and 63% QoQ, with blended ATF around ₹140-150 per litre in Q1FY27 versus ₹85-90 pre-war.
Middle East departures recovered to north of 90% of the pre-war ~150 daily departures by end-June, after falling to 20-30 at the peak of the crisis.
International was close to 33% of capacity in Q1FY27, with a 40% target by 2030.
Customs authority issued an order confirming additional customs duty demand on import of ATF along with a ₹3.50 crore fine and penalty for May 2024 to August 2025.

timeline.summary: InterGlobe Aviation received a DGCA warning letter regarding December 2025 airfares, noting corrective refunds and no financial impact.
On April 30, 2026, Moody's completed a periodic review of InterGlobe Aviation's ratings without any credit action.
InterGlobe Aviation reported Q4FY26 revenue of ₹22,438.4 Cr and a net loss of ₹2,537 Cr, impacted by sharp foreign exchange losses.
Neerja Sharma shared the earnings call recording for Q4 Jan-Mar 2026 and FY 2025-26 on May 29, 2026, available at https://www.goindigo.in.

On 2 June 2026, InterGlobe Aviation said it will temporarily discontinue India–Manchester flights from 31 August 2026 and return one of six damp-leased Boeing 787-9s to Norse Atlantic Airways, citing airspace constraints, ATF costs and forex volatility.
InterGlobe Aviation held its Q4FY26 earnings call on May 29, 2026, reporting a net loss of ₹2,537 Cr and appointing Willie Walsh as CEO.
InterGlobe Aviation announced the temporary suspension of flights to six international destinations from July to September 2026 as part of network optimization.
On June 8, 2026, InterGlobe Aviation hosted its Analyst Day 2026, presenting long-term growth targets and strategic roadmaps.
IndiGo reported a Q1FY27 net loss of ₹2.4 bn against a ₹21.8 bn profit a year earlier as fuel CASK rose 80%, and guided Q2FY27 capacity flat with PRASK up over 25%.
InterGlobe Aviation disclosed a customs order confirming a ₹3.50 Cr duty demand, fine, and penalty for the period of May 2024 to August 2025.
